stem: A nurse reviews a 2026 heart-failure consultation note that classifies the client's syndrome as heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF). Which statement is most accurate?

options.A: A preserved ejection fraction does not exclude heart failure; the diagnosis requires a clinical heart-failure syndrome supported by structural or functional cardiac abnormality and objective evidence such as elevated natriuretic peptides or cardiogenic congestion.
options.B: HFpEF means the heart is structurally and functionally normal because the ejection fraction is preserved.
options.C: HFpEF is diagnosed from a preserved ejection fraction alone, even when there are no heart-failure symptoms, signs, biomarkers, or evidence of congestion.
options.D: HFpEF and HFrEF are physiologically identical syndromes, so ejection-fraction phenotype and supporting diagnostic evidence do not affect evaluation or management.

rationale: The 2026 Second Universal Definition of Heart Failure moves away from rigid ejection-fraction cutoffs as the sole basis for phenotype classification and emphasizes a clinical HF syndrome caused by structural or functional cardiac abnormality with supporting objective evidence. The 2026 ACC HFpEF pathway likewise defines HF using symptoms/signs from cardiac abnormality plus elevated natriuretic peptides or objective cardiogenic congestion. Therefore, a preserved EF does not mean normal cardiac function or diagnose HF by itself. B and C equate preserved EF with either normality or sufficient diagnostic proof, and D ignores clinically meaningful phenotype differences.
educational_objective: Recognize that HFpEF is a clinical heart-failure syndrome supported by cardiac abnormality and objective evidence; preserved ejection fraction alone neither excludes nor establishes heart failure.
source_organization: American Heart Association / American College of Cardiology / European Society of Cardiology / World Heart Federation, in collaboration with HFSA, HFA and JHFS; American College of Cardiology
source_document_title: Second Universal Definition of Heart Failure (2026); Management of Heart Failure With Preserved Ejection Fraction: 2026 ACC Expert Consensus Decision Pathway
source_version_date: Universal Definition published 2026-06-29; ACC HFpEF pathway published 2026-07-23
source_locator: Second Universal Definition of HF → Top Things to Know items 1 and 3: 2026 framework groups HF into reduced, preserved, and improved EF categories and moves away from arbitrary rigid numeric LVEF thresholds. 2026 ACC HFpEF Expert Consensus → Assumptions and Definitions: HF requires symptoms/signs caused by structural or functional cardiac abnormality plus at least one of elevated natriuretic peptides or objective evidence of cardiogenic pulmonary/systemic congestion; HFpEF evaluation must distinguish mimics and cannot rest on EF alone.
source_claim_supported: Directly supports interpreting preserved EF within a clinical HF syndrome rather than equating HFpEF with normal cardiac function or diagnosing it from ejection fraction alone.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Physiological Integrity → Physiological Adaptation → Alterations in Body Systems/Pathophysiology: identify pathophysiology related to acute and chronic conditions and apply knowledge of altered cardiac function when caring for clients.
blueprint_topic: Physiological Adaptation — contemporary interpretation of HFpEF and heart-failure pathophysiology
correction_summary: Substantively updated the source item. The original answer reduced HFpEF to 'preserved EF plus diastolic dysfunction' and contrasted it with rigid HFrEF thresholds. A June 2026 multisociety universal definition now explicitly moves away from rigid numeric EF anchors. The final item tests the safer current principle that preserved EF does not equal normal function and that HF requires a clinical syndrome with objective supporting evidence.

audit_findings.source_authority: Current June 2026 multisociety universal-definition consensus plus July 2026 ACC HFpEF expert consensus pathway.
audit_findings.currentness: These 2026 documents are newer than the 2022 HF EF-classification framework and directly address contemporary HF/HFpEF definition at the audit date.

claim_by_claim.stem: The note is explicitly a 2026 classification scenario, so the current universal definition and HFpEF pathway apply.
claim_by_claim.A: Correct because preserved EF does not exclude a symptomatic HF syndrome and objective biomarker/congestion evidence is part of the current HF definition.
claim_by_claim.B: Incorrect because preserved EF does not imply normal structural or functional cardiac physiology.
claim_by_claim.C: Incorrect because EF alone is insufficient to diagnose HF; clinical syndrome and objective support are required.
claim_by_claim.D: Incorrect because reduced and preserved EF remain distinct clinically actionable phenotypes even though rigid numeric cutoffs are de-emphasized.
claim_by_claim.rationale: Avoids an outdated universal LVEF threshold and avoids reducing HFpEF to one mechanism such as isolated impaired relaxation.
claim_by_claim.educational_objective: Specific to current HFpEF diagnostic interpretation.

audit_findings.distractor_audit: B tests preserved-EF-equals-normal misconception, C EF-only diagnosis, and D phenotype equivalence. Each is plausible and distinct.
audit_findings.ambiguity_and_second_answer: Only A incorporates both preserved EF and the required clinical/objective HF evidence. No other choice is defensible under 2026 definitions.
audit_findings.cueing: All options are explanatory statements about HFpEF rather than obviously unrelated physiology.
audit_findings.blueprint: Physiological Adaptation remains appropriate because the item tests pathophysiologic interpretation of chronic cardiac dysfunction.
audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: Re-audited after discovering the June 2026 Second Universal Definition and July 2026 ACC HFpEF pathway. The older rigid ≥50% versus ≤40% contrast was intentionally not retained as the final construct. A reflects the newest authoritative framework and has no unresolved conflict.
